q: After a key rotation, every request fails with HTTP 403. Your wrapper keeps retrying with exponential backoff. What is wrong?

options.text: Nothing; backoff will succeed once the new key propagates
403 is terminal; fix the credentials or permissions instead
The backoff is too short; 403s need much longer waits
403 means overload, so it should switch to a fallback model

explain: Ask whether the exact same request could plausibly work later. A 403 is a permissions failure, so it is terminal and retrying can't help. Retriable errors are 429, 529 and transient 5xx.

q: Under peak load you get HTTP 429 responses with a `retry-after` header. Your code retries immediately in a tight loop, and the errors get worse. What should it do?

options.text: Retry immediately but from several threads to spread load
Honor `retry-after`, back off with jitter, and cap retries
Treat 429 as terminal and fail every request right away
Switch to a larger model, which has a separate rate limit

explain: 429 is retriable, but tight-loop retries deepen the rate limit. Honor `retry-after` when it is present, otherwise use exponential backoff with jitter, and cap the attempts with a clean fallback.

q: A support answer is wrong. The trace shows the retrieval step returned an empty list, so the prompt sent to Claude had no policy text. Where is the fault?

options.text: In the model, which should have said it lacked the policy
In the retrieval step, upstream of the model call
In the prompt wording, which needs a stronger instruction
In the model choice, since a larger model would know the policy

explain: The trace shows each step's inputs and outputs, and here the break happened at retrieval, before the model was called. A factual failure on retrieved content points at the retrieval step; changing the prompt or model would not fix a missing document.

q: Your error handler meets an error code you have never seen and can't tell whether it is retriable. What does the course recommend?

options.text: Retry it with backoff, since most errors turn out to be transient
Treat it as terminal so it fails loudly until you understand it
Return an empty result so the user isn't shown an error message
Retry it forever, since giving up would lose the user's request

explain: When unsure, treat it as terminal. A wrongly terminal error fails loudly and gets fixed, while a wrongly retriable one hammers the service and burns the retry budget. Never hide a failure as an empty result.
